note: Fixed term list for the per-pair glossaries (docs/seo/tasks/01-measurement-harness.md §1). The harness records the translation the engine ACTUALLY produces for each of these — verbatim, not scored by a model — and that output becomes the glossary on the pair page. These are chosen because they are the terms that get mistranslated in ways a bilingual speaker would notice and a dictionary would not: business senses that differ from the everyday sense of the same word.

procurement.trap: Often rendered as a generic 'order', losing the document sense.
Often becomes 'late order', which is not the same thing.
A proper noun that must not be translated.

finance.trap: A payment term, not a quantity. Commonly mangled.
Has no direct equivalent in several target languages.
The everyday sense is physical agitation; the business sense is customer loss.

legal.trap: The acronym NDA is often kept in English; record which.
Legal term of art; a literal rendering changes the meaning.
Recent GDPR-specific term; coverage is uneven.
Already French; should pass through untouched.
Frequently conflated with 'guarantee', which is a different obligation.
The contract sense, not the task sense.

delivery.trap: Idiomatic; a literal rendering is meaningless.
SLA acronym handling varies by language.
The everyday sense is physical; the technical sense is a reversion.
Collides hard with the athletic sense.
Latin already; the medical sense may leak through.

people.trap: Often left in English; record whether it is.
Commonly mistranslated as a document rather than a person.
The legal category differs by jurisdiction, so the natural term differs too.
